title: RCGP: An Automatic Synthesis Framework for Reversible Quantum-Flux-Parametron Logic Circuits based on Efficient Cartesian Genetic Programming
problem: Designing large-scale reversible quantum-flux-parametron (RQFP) logic circuits is challenging due to distinctive logic functions and structures, and existing exact synthesis methods cannot scale to practical circuit sizes.
motivation: Reversible computing offers a promising approach to reduce energy dissipation in quantum computing systems.
method: RCGP uses Cartesian genetic programming (an evolutionary algorithm that combines modular building blocks) to automatically design reversible quantum-flux-parametron (RQFP) logic circuits. The algorithm creates many circuit variations and keeps designs that minimize gate count (total logic operations) and garbage outputs (extra qubits produced as byproducts). To ensure correctness, it uses simulation and formal verification to confirm that each new circuit variant functions identically to its parent.
key_novelty: The framework uses Cartesian genetic programming — an evolutionary algorithm combining modular building blocks — to automatically design large-scale reversible quantum-flux-parametron logic circuits.
contributions: RCGP framework for automatic synthesis of large-scale RQFP logic circuits
Integration of circuit simulation and formal verification for functional equivalence checking
Optimization considering RQFP-specific characteristics to minimize gates and garbage outputs
Demonstrated scalability beyond existing exact logic synthesis methods
limitations: The abstract does not discuss specific limitations of the proposed approach.
primary_theme: Automatic synthesis for reversible quantum circuits
